title: CMake+tools: Automatically generate some of our dissector lists
description:
Add generate-dissector-lists.py, which automatically generates our lists 
of ASN.1 dissectors and public headers. Headers must contain one or more
of the following in order to be included in the list:

- Functions marked WS_DLL_PUBLIC
- Structs whose names contain "tap_"
- The string "PUBLIC_HEADER"

This automatically adds headers that should obviously be installed and 
provides an easy way to add non-obvious headers.

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 5e2d5581 - DRAFT: CMake+tools: Automatically generate some of our dissector lists
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22579/diffs?diff_id=1586345925&start_sha=e427304e41aa1457516d957de1363ba900f8c90a)

This only installs headers that contain `WS_DLL_PUBLIC`, which is significantly reduced from the previous list. It should be easy to provide a way to manually flag headers for export, but I'm open to suggestions on the specifics of that. Would matching for a specific comment, e.g. `// PUBLIC_HEADER` work?

The big thing that we're losing with this approach is dissectors that have headers strictly for tap data or just data structures to pass between dissectors have no WS_DLL_PUBLIC label. Is this aimed as a "general reset" to then expect developers with third-party plugins to submit patches to say, "I need that header!"?

I'm not strictly opposed to this approach, just asking the question.  Because the other side is we probably have several dissector header files that exist because developers were taught that structure definitions just go in header files.
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/21904#note_2829154678

I'd like to minimize our exported headers as much as possible, so this is definitely a general reset. As !22568 shows, the more headers we have in our public API, the more likely it is that we're going to run into difficulties backporting fixes.

> The big thing that we're losing with this approach is dissectors that have headers strictly for tap data or just data structures to pass between dissectors

It looks like we might be able to pick up most of the tap struts by matching for `struct .*tap_`. Forcing a consistent naming convention for those wouldn't be a bad side effect.
Definitely like the idea of some naming conventions for taps and data passed between dissectors.  Was hoping to spot check the list of no longer included header files, but ATM the list is a bit big.
OK, I expanded the pattern to `(^\s*WS_DLL_PUBLIC\b|\bstruct\s.*tap_|\bPUBLIC_HEADER\b)`. That increased the header count from 108 to 120.
I guess I was hoping there would be a little more... Do you think changes like adding more PUBLIC_HEADER or renaming tap structures should be handled outside this MR?

Yeah. This is kind of like trying to trim down a set of firewall rules that have accumulated over 25 years. I'm leaning toward trimming the list down to what should obviously be there and let people who need them request or contribute additions. I plan on posting a message to wireshark-dev and the developer-den Discord channel once this is merged.

> [!note]
>
> Is this aimed as a "general reset" to then expect developers with third-party plugins to submit patches to say, "I need that header!"?

This was mine concern here, but after trying out the change on my internal build it continue happy, so it's fine or I was just luck (?)

Do you have a bunch of third-party plugins or just "internal built-in dissectors" that have access to the full dissector directory?  I was thinking about this, but companies that have "full internal builds" of Wireshark probably aren't affected by this.  It's just those that want to distribute "standalone" third-party plugins, so then the list of "public headers" needed is probably much smaller.

Some third-party plugins but most are internal built-in dissectors, however many utilizes upstream public headers, even usage which is not perform by any dissector here (which comment in .h header has been added regards to usage so it is not remove, like file-pcapng.h and packet-gtpv2.h)
assigned to @rbalint

`packet-smb2.h` includes `packet-ntlmssp.h`. The latter doesn't have any `WS_DLL_PUBLIC` functions, but does define ` NTLMSSP_KEY_LEN` which the former header uses. We might need to do some kind of dependency resolution.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22579/diffs?diff_id=1586405213&start_sha=5e2d5581d34b1f0fd3bc8a0e1fe233e36b929937#244f01729cabaa1dcbc8569b0886d5529384718f_312_315)
Done. It now recursively adds packet-*.h includes.

Per https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22579#note_2930219419, what about also including headers that other dissector C files include (presumably because there are shared data structures)?
Wouldn't that end up exporting all of hour dissector headers?

You'd have to exclude the "base" C file, i.e. packet-cip.h would only be included if it's included by something _other than_ packet-cip.c.  (packet-cip.h is one I'm watching because I'm pretty sure there are third-party plugins for it.  So I would also nominate it for testing the // PUBLIC_HEADER mnemonic).

That's correct. If this is merged it will greatly reduce the number of headers in future libwireshark-dev packages. I wish the GitLab UI had a more obvious way to ping someone.
unassigned @rbalint

Instead of editing CMakeList.txt in place with generate-dissector-lists.py I'd change generate-dissector-lists.py to write the list of files to its output and include that output with something like `execute_process(COMMAND tools/generate-dissector-lists.py public OUTPUT_VARIABLE DISSECTOR_PUBLIC_HEADERS` .
This way the list can't go out of sync in the repo. Developers can still check the list by running the generator.

Wouldn't that keep the build environment from regenerating itself when there are updates, similar to the reason you shouldn't use [file(GLOB ...)](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/command/file.html#glob)? That would also add a Python invocation to each `cmake` run, which would slow down configuration even more on Windows. It would be easy enough to run this by hand, and I was planning on adding it to the weekly update job.

Well, I think there are no really good solution for the problem. Regenerating the list is clean, but I understand if it is too slow on Windows. 
I ran a few tests and it is noticable on Linux, too:

```
rbalint@nano:~/projects/deb/wireshark.git$ time tools/generate-dissector-lists.py 
Found 121 public header files.
Found 130 ASN.1 source files.

real	0m0,428s
user	0m0,421s
sys	0m0,079s
rbalint@nano:~/projects/deb/wireshark.git$ time firebuild tools/generate-dissector-lists.py 
Found 121 public header files.
Found 130 ASN.1 source files.

real	0m0,797s
user	0m0,518s
sys	0m0,267s
rbalint@nano:~/projects/deb/wireshark.git$ time firebuild tools/generate-dissector-lists.py 
Found 121 public header files.
Found 130 ASN.1 source files.

real	0m0,068s
user	0m0,029s
sys	0m0,039s
```

The run can be cached, but that does not work on Windows either.

IMO it would be better running a check in CI and throwing an error when the regenerated CMakeLists.txt does not match the committed version to cache discrepancies earlier.
Thanks, I added a CI check.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+#
+# Wireshark - Network traffic analyzer
+# By Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>
+# Copyright 1998 Gerald Combs
+#
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+#
+'''\
+Generate the DISSECTOR_PUBLIC_HEADERS and CLEAN_ASN1_DISSECTOR_SRC lists in epan/dissectors/CMakeLists.txt.
+
+For DISSECTOR_PUBLIC_HEADERS, each header must contain at least one exported function.
+'''
+
+import concurrent.futures
+import os
+import os.path
+import re
+import sys
+
+from enum import Enum
+
+State = Enum('State', ['Normal', 'InAsn1Dissectors', 'InPublicHeaders'])
+
+DISSECTORS_PATH = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', 'epan', 'dissectors'))
+CMAKELISTS_TXT = os.path.join(DISSECTORS_PATH, 'CMakeLists.txt')
+THIS_FILE = os.path.basename(__file__)
+
+PACKET_SOURCE_FILE_PATTERN = r'^packet-.*\.c$'
+ASN1_SOURCE_PATTERN = r'Generated automatically by the ASN.1 to Wireshark dissector compiler'
+
+PACKET_HEADER_FILE_PATTERN = r'^(file|packet)-.*\.h$'
+PUBLIC_HEADER_PATTERN = r'(^\s*WS_DLL_PUBLIC\b|\bstruct\s.*tap_|\bPUBLIC_HEADER\b)'
+PACKET_HEADER_INCLUDE_PATTERN = r'^\s*#\s*include\s.*\b(packet-.*\.h)\b'
+
+MIN_ASN1_SOURCE_COUNT = 130 # 130 on 2025-12-03
+MIN_HEADER_COUNT = 120 # 121 on 2025-12-03
+
+def exit_msg(msg=None, status=1):
+    if msg is not None:
+        sys.stderr.write(msg + '\n\n')
+    sys.stderr.write(__doc__ + '\n')
+    sys.exit(status)
+
+def search_asn1_source(source_file):
+    with open (os.path.join(DISSECTORS_PATH, source_file)) as f:
+        if re.search(ASN1_SOURCE_PATTERN, f.read(512), re.MULTILINE):
+            return source_file
+    return None
+
+def get_asn1_sources():
+    '''Search for public packet-*.h headers.
+    Returns a list of filenames.
+    '''
+    packet_sources = [e.name for e in os.scandir(DISSECTORS_PATH) if e.is_file() and re.match(PACKET_SOURCE_FILE_PATTERN, e.name) ]
+
+    asn1_sources = []
+    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
+        sources = executor.map(search_asn1_source, packet_sources)
+        asn1_sources.extend([s for s in sources if s is not None])
+
+    if len(asn1_sources) < MIN_ASN1_SOURCE_COUNT:
+        exit_msg(f'Too few ASN.1 sources. Found {len(asn1_sources)}, need {MIN_ASN1_SOURCE_COUNT}')
+
+    print(f'Found {len(asn1_sources)} ASN.1 source files.')
+    return sorted(asn1_sources, key=str.lower)
+
+def get_packet_includes(header_file, depth=0):
+    if depth > 10:
+        return []
+    includes = []
+    with open (os.path.join(DISSECTORS_PATH, header_file)) as f:
+        for include in re.findall(PACKET_HEADER_INCLUDE_PATTERN, f.read(), re.MULTILINE):
+            includes.append(include)
+            includes.extend(get_packet_includes(include, depth+1))
+    return includes
+
+def search_packet_header(header_file):
+    with open (os.path.join(DISSECTORS_PATH, header_file)) as f:
+        if re.search(PUBLIC_HEADER_PATTERN, f.read(), re.MULTILINE):
+            header_files = [header_file]
+            header_files.extend(get_packet_includes(header_file))
+            return header_files
+    return []
+
+def get_public_headers():
+    '''Search for public packet-*.h headers.
+    Returns a list of filenames.
+    '''
+    packet_headers = [e.name for e in os.scandir(DISSECTORS_PATH) if e.is_file() and re.match(PACKET_HEADER_FILE_PATTERN, e.name) ]
+
+    public_headers = []
+    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
+        header_lists = executor.map(search_packet_header, packet_headers)
+        for header_list in header_lists:
+            public_headers.extend(header_list)
+
+    if len(public_headers) < MIN_HEADER_COUNT:
+        exit_msg(f'Too few public headers. Found {len(public_headers)}, need {MIN_HEADER_COUNT}')
+
+    print(f'Found {len(public_headers)} public header files.')
+    return sorted(set(public_headers), key=str.lower)
+
+
+def main():
+    warning = f'# Do not edit. Automatically generated by {THIS_FILE}'
+    public_headers = [warning] + get_public_headers()
+    asn1_sources = get_asn1_sources()
+
+    cmakelists_f = open(CMAKELISTS_TXT, 'r')
+    cm_lines = list(cmakelists_f)
+    cmakelists_f = open(CMAKELISTS_TXT, 'w+')
+    cm_out = ''
+    state = State.Normal
+
+    for line in cm_lines:
+        if state == State.Normal:
+            cm_out += line
+            if re.match(r'^\s*set\s*\(\s*DISSECTOR_PUBLIC_HEADERS', line):
+                state = State.InPublicHeaders
+                cm_out += ''.join([f'\t{ph}\n' for ph in public_headers])
+            elif re.match(r'^\s*set\s*\(\s*CLEAN_ASN1_DISSECTOR_SRC', line):
+                state = State.InAsn1Dissectors
+                cm_out += f'\t{warning}\n'
+                cm_out += ''.join([f'\t${{CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}}/{af}\n' for af in asn1_sources])
+        elif re.match(r'^\s*\)', line):
+            state = State.Normal
+            cm_out += line
+
+    cmakelists_f.write(cm_out)
+    cmakelists_f.close()
+
+#
+# On with the show
+#
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

commits_data.message:
CMake+tools: Automatically generate some of our dissector lists

Add generate-dissector-lists.py, which automatically generates our lists
of ASN.1 dissectors and public headers. Headers must contain one or more
of the following in order to be included in the list:

- Functions marked WS_DLL_PUBLIC
- Structs whose names contain "tap_"
- The string "PUBLIC_HEADER"

This automatically adds headers that should obviously be installed and
provides an easy way to add non-obvious headers.
